styles.blurb: Central Market, laneway bars and winery day trips.

styles.label: Beach

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums on North Terrace and the Adelaide Oval.

stays.why: Walk to the Central Market, North Terrace museums and the free tram zone. Best base without a car.
Quiet streets, pubs and cafés, a short walk or bus to the city and the Oval.
Beachfront stays with the tram running straight into the city.
Cheaper rooms near the docks, dolphin cruises and the railway museum; a train ride to the CBD.

food: Start at Adelaide Central Market: graze on cheese, smallgoods, pastries and coffee. Many stalls close early afternoon, so go in the morning.
Try a pie floater or a bakery pie, and a Farmers Union iced coffee, a local habit.
The Barossa and McLaren Vale wine regions are day trips from the city. Book a tour or a driver if you plan to taste.
Laneways off Hindley Street and Peel Street have small bars and cheap eats. Book popular places ahead on weekends.
Seafood is best near the coast at Glenelg or Port Adelaide. Check the day's catch and prices on the board.
more_time: Add a day in the Barossa Valley: cellar doors, big red wines and long lunches, about an hour's drive each way.
Take the ferry to Kangaroo Island for wildlife and coast, but it needs at least one overnight, not a day trip.
Swap a city afternoon for the Adelaide Hills: Hahndorf's German-style main street and lookout stops, about 30–40 minutes by car.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Central Market, North Terrace museums and a Glenelg beach afternoon; add a night for a wine-region day trip.

month_notes: January: hot and dry, highs near 28°C. Beach days are great; start walks early.
February: the driest month, only about 2 rain days. Warm evenings suit outdoor dining.
March: still warm at 25°C, with a few more rain days. Good all-round month.
April: mild at 21°C with about 7 rain days. Bring a light jacket for evenings.
May: cooler at 17°C and wetter, around 11 rain days. Plan indoor sights and cafés.
June: cool and wet, highs near 15°C with about 12 rain days. Pack a rain jacket.
July: the coldest month, highs near 14°C and lows around 8°C. Wettest stretch, about 13 rain days.
August: similar to July, cold and showery. Museums and markets are good choices.
September: warming to 17°C but still about 11 rain days. Carry a compact umbrella.
October: mild at 21°C with about 8 rain days. Good for walking and the hills.
November: warm at 23°C and drier, about 7 rain days. A strong month for the beach.
December: hot and dry, highs near 26°C. Book restaurants and beach spots ahead.

climate_guide.summary: Mediterranean-style climate: hot, dry summers and cool, wetter winters. Rain is spread over the cooler months.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Warm to hot days around 23–28°C and low rain. Ideal for beaches, the hills and outdoor dining.

items.title: Wettest: June to August
items.text: About 12–13 rain days a month and highs near 14–15°C. Pack a rain jacket and plan indoor stops.

items.title: Cool winters
items.text: July lows drop to about 8°C. Mornings and evenings feel cold; bring layers.

items.title: Beach weather
items.text: Best from December to March. By June to August the sea and air are cold for swimming.

items.title: Mild shoulder months
items.text: April, October and November are comfortable at about 21–23°C with moderate rain. Good for walking and wine regions.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Summer: light clothes, hat and sunscreen. Winter: warm layers, a waterproof jacket and an umbrella.

transit.best: Walk or take the free city tram in the centre; use the tram to Glenelg and trains for Port Adelaide.

modes.text: Adelaide Metro runs trains, trams and buses with one tap-and-pay system. Trams and some city buses are free within the city centre. The tram runs to Glenelg.
Part of the same Adelaide Metro tap-and-pay system. Some city buses are free in the centre.
Taxis use the meter; airport pickups add a small surcharge. Uber and other ride apps operate across the city.
Driving is easy but parking in the CBD costs money. Useful for the Barossa, McLaren Vale and the hills.
The city is flat and good for walking and cycling.
Adelaide Metro trains are part of the same tap-and-pay system. Useful for Port Adelaide and outer suburbs.
